# Codex Continuity

Codex Continuity is an unofficial, experimental, open-source Windows utility that keeps Codex agent threads alive while the desktop UI updates or restarts. It runs the official `codex app-server` outside the desktop process tree and reconnects the desktop over `ws://127.0.0.1:45123`.

## Safe install plan

Download the bootstrapper, then inspect its mutation-free JSON plan:

```powershell
$i="$env:TEMP\codex-continuity-install.ps1"
curl.exe -fsSL https://github.com/YesterdaysLemon/codex-continuity/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -o $i
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $i -Plan -Json
```

The plan reports the exact release asset and checksum URLs, whether the isolated self-test will run, whether the optional tray is enabled, and `restartsCodex: false`.

## Install

After reviewing the plan:

```powershell
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $i -StartNow
```

Use `-NoTray` for a headless install. The bootstrapper verifies the release SHA-256 before execution and never restarts the Codex desktop app. If Codex is already open, Continuity reserves its gated endpoint, keeps the second app-server off, and waits for the observed desktop processes to close naturally.

## Installed CLI, verification, and removal

Installation adds `CodexContinuity` to the user PATH. Open a new PowerShell window before invoking it by name.

```powershell
CodexContinuity status
CodexContinuity probe
CodexContinuity attach
CodexContinuity update-policy --enable
CodexContinuity repair
CodexContinuity uninstall
```

Automatic activation remains off by default. `update-policy --enable` opts into applying an already verified staged Continuity build only after a 30-second stable idle proof. The supervisor changes while the private backend and Codex desktop remain running; exact thread IDs, desktop identity, and reconnection must verify or Continuity rolls back. Re-run the command to retry a failed generation, or use `update-policy --disable` to keep updates staged.

Uninstall restores only configuration still owned by Continuity and never stops a running backend. Installed files and logs are removed at the next Windows sign-in. The supported v0.6.0 release target is Windows 11 x64 only; no macOS or Linux build is available. See the repository README and SECURITY.md before production use.
